claims.text: The owner gave Hacking Portugal as the keynote at BSidesLisbon on 11 November 2016; the video is 49 minutes.
claims.quote: I gave Hacking Portugal as the keynote at BSidesLisbon on 11 November 2016; the video is 49 minutes.

claims.text: The keynote had 103 slides and became a book three weeks later.
claims.quote: The BSidesLisbon keynote, 103 slides, then a book.

claims.text: If the word hack means to solve problems, then Hacking Portugal means to find innovative ways to solve existing problems.
claims.quote: If the word 'hack' means to solve problems, then 'Hacking Portugal' means to find innovative was to solve existing problems.

claims.text: The Leanpub book has 17 chapters, 75 pages and 14,487 words, is licensed CC BY 4.0, and still says 95% complete, last updated on 1 December 2016, the day it was published.
claims.quote: 17 chapters, 75 pages, 14,487 words, licensed CC BY 4.0, with a paperback on Amazon

claims.text: The book's introduction even gives the wrong date for the talk, 9 November.
claims.quote: Its introduction even gives the wrong date for the talk, 9 November.

claims.text: The talk opened with a Portuguese network hostile to insecure code: make it hard to create, publish or host insecure apps and devices in Portugal, by regulation, market pressure and a community that attacks vulnerable code before criminals do.
claims.quote: make it hard to create, publish or host insecure apps and devices in Portugal, by regulation, by market pressure and by a community that attacks vulnerable code before criminals do

claims.text: A 2016 scan of the country's exposed systems asked how secure Portugal was; the honest answer was insecure, but currently safe: not yet attacked at scale.
claims.quote: The honest answer was insecure, but currently safe: not yet attacked at scale.

claims.text: The regulation arrived from Europe: the Cyber Resilience Act's reporting duty since 11 September 2026, its security requirements in 2027, and Portugal's own cybersecurity law in force in April 2026.
claims.quote: The regulation arrived, from Europe.

claims.text: That is close to the Clear Software Act on slide 83, like the Clean Air Act but focused on code quality and security.
claims.quote: like the 'Clean Air Act', but focused on code quality and security

claims.text: The Portuguese Hacking Service: update the old compulsory military service into a hacking service for 15 to 21 year olds, paid for by moving a share of the military budget to cyber.
claims.quote: update the old compulsory military service into a hacking service for 15 to 21 year olds

claims.text: Around the service: a national hackathon league, teams sponsored to go to DefCon, and hacking taught the way Portugal teaches football.
claims.quote: a national hackathon league, teams sponsored to go to DefCon, and hacking taught the way Portugal teaches football

claims.text: As far as the owner knows, none of the service or the league happened in that form.
claims.quote: As far as I know, none of this happened in that form.

claims.text: A Hacking Service in 2026 would teach young people to direct agents against Portugal's own systems, with a mandate that says what they may and may not touch, since with agents a 16-year-old can explore a system by talking to it.
claims.quote: A Hacking Service in 2026 would teach young people to direct agents against Portugal's own systems, with a mandate that says what they may and may not touch.

claims.text: Code as a national asset: a Code Made in Portugal brand, OpenSource.pt with all government-paid code released under an open source licence, a Ministry of Code, a national bug bounty, and cyber security treated as public health.
claims.quote: All code written (and paid) for Government agencies to be released under an Open Source license

claims.text: In 2026 Portugal released Amália, a national language model for European Portuguese, as open source, built on the European EuroLLM model, which is the spirit of OpenSource.pt.
claims.quote: a national language model for European Portuguese, as open source, built on the European EuroLLM model

claims.text: The Ministry of Code and the national bug bounty are still ideas.
claims.quote: The Ministry of Code and the national bug bounty are still ideas.

claims.text: The public health analogy has grown more apt: Europe now treats software defects as a liability, from December, under the Product Liability Directive.
claims.quote: Europe now treats software defects as a liability, from December, under the Product Liability Directive

claims.text: The talk ended with a choice between Portugal as a garden for Europe and a technology powerhouse; the book argued it is easier in a small country with fewer agendas and fewer lobby groups.
claims.quote: more likely to have fewer agendas and fewer lobby groups wielding influence

claims.text: What the owner got wrong is the timescale and the idea that it would start from security; it may start from language and AI, where Portugal has just made a real move.
claims.quote: It did not start from security; it may start from language and AI, where Portugal has just made a real move.

claims.text: A book needs a feedback loop that a talk does not, which is why the next edition will be built from articles like this one, read before they are bound.
claims.quote: the next edition will be built from articles like this one, read before they are bound

claims.text: With agents everybody can now build software by talking, which makes the talk's central claim, that a small country can choose to lead in code, more possible than it was.
claims.quote: Everybody can build now; a small country can choose to lead.

claims.text: A new edition of Hacking Portugal for Web Summit in November would keep the structure and move the centre of gravity from application security to agents, language and sovereignty.
claims.quote: from application security to agents, language and sovereignty

claims.text: As far as I know means the owner did not survey it; some of these ideas may exist in a form he missed.
claims.quote: Some of these ideas may exist in a form I missed.

claims.text: The Clear Software Act is an analogy: the CRA is the EU's law, not the owner's.
claims.quote: The CRA is the EU's law, not mine.

claims.text: The commentary is the owner's, now; the slides are from 2016, unchanged.
claims.quote: The slides are from 2016, unchanged.
